newsitem.title: USA: Court denies motions to delay Oklahoma bomb trial.
newsitem.headline: Court denies motions to delay Oklahoma bomb trial.

text.p: A federal Appeals Court on Friday denied two requests by Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh to delay the scheduled beginning of the trial on Monday.

The Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit dismissed McVeigh's request to delay the start of the trial in order for him to obtain intelligence information from various government agencies and dismissed a second request to delay so that McVeigh could challenge a Victim Rights Act.

The two Appeals Court decisions were handed down three days before the scheduled start of the trial. McVeigh is charged with the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City. The bombing killed 168 people.

This week McVeigh's lawyers sought delays in the trial for three different reasons. On Tuesday, they sought a delay and an order from the court to compel the government to hand over intelligence information from various government agencies that the defense said would help its case.

On Wednesday, the lawyers went to the Appeals Court again seeking a delay to give McVeigh an opportunity to challenge a victim rights law that would allow victims of the bombing to both view the proceedings and testify at the penalty phase of the case.
On Friday, McVeigh's lawyers sought a delay, saying pre-trial publicity would prevent a fair hearing. There has been no decision from the Appeals Court on that request.
